source.title: From Local to Global to Mechanistic: An iERF-Centered Unified Framework for Interpreting Vision Models
source.authors: Yearim Kim; Sang-Yu Han; N. Kwak

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies interpretation and spatial grounding of SAE latents, but does not test whether increasing dictionary size produces related, partitioning feature splits, or any of the listed challenges to that claim.
record.gate_note: The paper trains Matryoshka SAEs for CAFE and reports insertion-test and qualitative results about latent attribution and spatial non-locality. Those results do not measure feature splitting or the relationship between smaller- and larger-dictionary latents. The related SAE-latent results are recorded as none-version rows; results on SRD and ICAT are outside the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper trains Matryoshka SAEs on CLIP ViT-L/14 layers as a tool and reports only the faithfulness of its own attribution method (CAFE insertion AUC) and qualitative non-locality of latents. It never varies dictionary size, compares parent/child latents, measures absorption, or tests whether Matryoshka SAEs change splitting. SAEs are also compared with k-means and dictionary learning at a fixed 8x overcompleteness (Tab. III), but only on reconstruction error and sparsity. No result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CAFE grounds SAE latents in pixel-level iERF evidence, recovers activations faster in insertion tests, and shows that non-local SAE features are rare early and more common in deeper layers. They draw no conclusion about feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses Matryoshka SAEs for feature interpretation but does not implement or compare an increasing-dictionary-size splitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The CAFE insertion results vary by attribution method: AttnLRP is reported to yield the strongest gains, followed closely by Integrated Gradients.

fits_no_version.finding: CAFE insertion AUC generally exceeds activation-ranking across CLIP ViT-L/14 layers; AttnLRP is best, then Integrated Gradients.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attribution-based grounding identifies the input evidence behind SAE latents more faithfully than top-activation ranking.

fits_no_version.finding: Spatially non-local SAE latents are rare in early ViT layers (mostly class-token features) and more common in later layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents in vision transformers become increasingly spatially decoupled from their evidence with depth.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The SAE-related findings are qualitative or summarized without numerical insertion AUC values in the text; the paper does not compare SAE dictionary sizes or test the splitting claim.
record.rows_left_out: SRD local-explanation comparisons and ICAT interlayer-attribution results were left out because they do not concern SAE feature splitting. Other qualitative CAFE examples are not separately tabulated because they illustrate the same non-locality and attribution-grounding result recorded in r2.

untested.parts: No variation of SAE dictionary size; no parent/child feature comparison, coverage or direction similarity.
No splitting analysis in large models or open SAE releases.
No nested feature families or hierarchy analysis among SAE latents.
No absorption measurement and no size or sparsity sweep.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no count of novel latents.
Matryoshka SAEs are used but not compared with standard SAEs on splitting.

record.verdict_notes: Changed the relation from discusses/T6 to uses_without_test/T4: the paper relies on Matryoshka SAEs as a tool and reports only its own method's performance. Splitting, absorption and canonical units are not mentioned. Monosemanticity (Bricken et al.) is cited only as a source for SAEs.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of increasing SAE dictionary sizes, feature directions, or whether child features partition a parent feature's inputs.
No test of the splitting pattern across large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families or whether they reflect a concept hierarchy.
No test of parent-child absorption, parent firing failures, or whether size or sparsity changes address absorption.
No decomposition comparison between larger- and smaller-SAE latents and no test for novel latents or canonical units.
No test that the SAE objective produces splitting, or that Matryoshka SAEs change or reduce splitting.

rows.subject: CLIP–ViT-L/14 encoder
rows.operation_detail: Compared insertion-test recovery of SAE latent activations using CAFE attribution against activation-ranking and alternative attribution methods.

conditions.value: 5 × 10^8 image patches from ImageNet-1K per transformer layer
insertion-curve AUC over images and features

rows.measure: Insertion-test AUC for recovering the original latent activation
rows.value: iERF-guided CAFE generally outperforms activation-ranking across layers; among CAFE variants, AttnLRP yields the strongest gains, followed closely by Integrated Gradients.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative summary; numerical AUC values are shown only in the figure. This evaluates attributional faithfulness, not feature splitting.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (CAFE) with baselines. It is a method-performance result, not a measure of feature splitting, so its state relative to the claim cannot be determined.

rows.subject: CLIP–ViT-L/14 encoder
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively examined SAE latent activation locations and their iERF evidence across transformer layers.

conditions.value: SAE features including Feature 14 at Layer 22, Feature 69 at Layer 20, and a Green Image class-token feature

rows.measure: Spatial localization of latent activations and iERF-grounded evidence
rows.value: The authors report that non-locality is rare in earlier layers and becomes more common in later layers; iERFs identify evidence that may be spatially displaced from the maximally activating token.
rows.note: Qualitative result about SAE latent localization, not about relationships between dictionary sizes or partitions of feature inputs.
rows.check: Qualitative spatial non-locality of SAE latents across layers. This is a different construct from splitting with dictionary size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
